content: 1. No evidence synthesis was commissioned for all adults regarding the benefits and harms of cognitive therapy in managing chronic primary low back pain in community-dwelling adults, including older adults aged 60 years and over. No trials were identified comparing cognitive therapy with placebo. 2. The benefits and harms of cognitive therapy in managing chronic primary low back pain in community-dwelling adults, including older adults aged 60 years and over, compared with no intervention, were not assessed due to the absence of trials. 3. Cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) is based on a multidimensional model of pain and aims to reduce pain and distress by modifying physical sensations, catastrophic thinking, and unhelpful behaviors. It may include education about the multidimensional nature of pain, identifying pain-eliciting and pain-aggravating situations, thoughts, and behaviors, and employing coping strategies and applied relaxation techniques. CBT integrates components of operant, respondent, and cognitive therapies, with a focus on goal-setting and activity increases to reduce feelings of helplessness and help individuals gain control over their pain experience. 4. The PICO structure for CBT includes community-dwelling adults aged 20 years and over with chronic primary low back pain, with or without leg pain, including older adults aged 60 years and over. Critical outcomes include pain, back-specific function/disability, general function/disability, health-related quality of life, psychosocial function, social participation, self-efficacy, and adverse events as reported in trials. 5. Judgments regarding equity, human rights, acceptability, and feasibility of interventions were made based on the experience of GDG (Guideline Development Group) members, as no evidence synthesis was commissioned or identified for all adults. 6. Mindfulness-based stress reduction (MBSR) therapy aims to reduce stress by fostering mindfulness, defined as non-judgmental, moment-by-moment acceptance of awareness. This intervention is free of cultural, religious, and ideological factors but is associated with the Buddhist origins of mindfulness. The PICO structure for MBSR includes community-dwelling adults aged 20 years and over with chronic primary low back pain, with or without leg pain, including older adults aged 60 years and over. 7. Risk of bias in studies was downgraded by two levels due to unclear or high risk across all studies regarding random sequence generation, allocation concealment, blinding of participants, care providers, and outcome assessment, incomplete outcome data, selective reporting, baseline group similarity, co-interventions, and compliance with the intervention. 8. Imprecision was downgraded by one level due to a low number of participants or wide confidence intervals consistent with the possibility of benefit and no effect. Inconsistency was not assessed in cases where only one study was included in the analysis. 9. Subgroup analyses were not performed, and all studies were conducted in high-income settings.
